title: Randomized Message-Locked Encryption Beyond XtESPKE
summary: A reported black-box barrier covers deterministic MLE but apparently not randomized MLE; build randomized MLE beyond XtESPKE or delimit what randomization can evade.

formal_statement.body: A black-box barrier to obtaining secure deterministic message-locked encryption (D-MLE) is reported to apply to D-MLE but, as far as the available evidence indicates, not to randomized message-locked encryption (R-MLE). The route noted for R-MLE under standard assumptions is XtESPKE, obtained by extending XtDPKE from an efficiently searchable public-key encryption (ES-PKE) scheme, which is weaker than deterministic searchable public-key encryption (D-PKE). The unresolved task is to construct an R-MLE scheme under standard assumptions that goes beyond this XtESPKE/ES-PKE approach, or to characterize the limits of using randomization to avoid the D-MLE barrier.

scope.domain: Design of deterministic and randomized message-locked encryption in the presence of black-box barriers.
parameters: XtESPKE from ES-PKE: the noted randomized MLE construction route
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct an R-MLE scheme under standard assumptions beyond the XtESPKE/ES-PKE route, or characterize how far randomization can avoid the D-MLE black-box barrier.

progress.summary: The source presents randomization as a potential way around the D-MLE black-box barrier under standard assumptions. It identifies XtESPKE from ES-PKE as the noted route and states that no approach beyond it is known.
citation_labels: Mihir Bellare et al., Message-Locked Encryption and Secure Deduplication
